Subject: Sudden drop in reserved throughput (FastPay production)

Hi Lauren —

We started seeing increased 503 errors and large tail latencies against the Redwood Dedicated endpoint tied to our reserved pool this morning. Key metrics:
- Sustained throughput at ~60% of our reserved commit for the last 3 hours (we expect 1,200 qps; seeing ~720 qps).
- Token latency 95p moved from ~300ms to ~1.1–1.3s.
- Error rate (5xx) from ~0.1% to 2.8%.

This is affecting our live payments validation flow; customers are timing out on multi-step flows. We escalated on our side but need immediate help — please confirm you are seeing this on your side and advise mitigation steps. I attached a short perf trace and some request IDs.

Thanks,
Rajiv

On Sun, Apr 18, 2027 at 09:37, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marissa / team — forwarding FastPay incident.

Adding initial triage: we've started collecting runtime traces from the FastPay pool and see concurrent allocation spikes on a subset of nodes. Initial hypothesis: autoscaler policies allowed transient burst instances to attach to a shared rack causing GPU scheduling pressure that reduced effective per-tenant throughput. We're also seeing an elevated KV cache miss rate for FastPay's request patterns which increases per-token compute.

Immediate actions executed (10:00 PDT):
- Enabled temporary routing to FastPay's warm spare pool (20% extra capacity) to reduce tail latencies (applied).
- Throttled non-critical background batch jobs running in the same region (applied).
- Captured kernel-level traces; attaching trace bundle to the internal incident.

We need engineering to validate whether reserved tokens are being enforced at the scheduler layer (not just admission control). Vivek, can you confirm if the scheduler honored the reserved share overnight?

Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden drop in reserved throughput (FastPay production)

Quick update from eng triage:
- Root cause (prelim): an autoscaler rollback from Apr 17 pushed a default burst policy that allowed shared workloads to co-locate on reserved-pool racks during brief scaling windows. That policy was intended for on-demand pools but was accidentally applied to dedicated auto policies in us-west-2. Result: GPU oversubscription => queueing => elevated 5xx and latency.
- We are seeing correct admission throttles in the front proxy, but downstream scheduler mis-accounted active slots during the transition period. This explains why the reserve appeared to be under-provisioned.

Mitigation plan (timeline):
- 11:30 PDT: revert autoscaler change (in progress).
- 12:00 PDT: force-failover FastPay workloads to the warm spare pool (already partly done by ops).
- 14:00 PDT: run a safety patch to reassert per-tenant scheduling quotas and add an immediate metric to alert on "effective reserved fulfillment".

ETA to restore to baseline: 2–4 hours assuming rollback and rebalancing succeed. If we see persistent kernel-level contention we'll open a hotfix for the scheduler later today.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure & Serving, Redwood Inference

Summary: FastPay (FP-2025-4789) has experienced a sustained ~40% shortfall vs reserved throughput for ~3+ hours with elevated 5xx and tail latency. Engineering identifies a misapplied autoscaler policy as the likely cause and has a rollback+rebalancing plan with 2–4 hour ETA to restore.

Risks and asks:
- If restoration slips beyond 6 hours we need to prepare an SLA remediation conversation and a draft credit scenario. Legal may want to pre-draft customer communications.
- Please prioritize a mitigation patch to hard-assert reserved shares in the scheduler today.
- Ask for a headcount/infra ops hold if we need rapid extra capacity in us-west-2 (budget impact to be assessed).

Rajiv — we apologize for the disruption. I'll continue to post updates every hour and will coordinate any customer comms with Legal and CS.

— Lauren

Rajiv / Anya —

Status update (final from this thread):
- Baseline throughput for your reserved pool has been restored to >98% of the committed level as of 15:15 PDT on 2027-04-22.
- Root cause: autoscaler rollback from Apr 17 that applied a shared burst policy to certain dedicated pools; fixed via rollback + scheduler safety patch.
- What we did:
  - Immediate routing to warm spare pool to stop customer impact (Apr 18)
  - Autoscaler policy rollback (Apr 18)
  - Hotfix to enforce per-tenant scheduling quotas + new metric and alert for "effective reserved fulfillment" (Apr 18–22)

Deliverables and next steps:
- By 2027-04-25: Post-mortem and timeline of changes with remediation plan to avoid recurrence (owner: Marissa Cole).
- By 2027-04-29: Follow-up validation run with FastPay synthetic traffic to prove sustained throughput under peak patterns (owner: Vivek Kulkarni).
- We've attached the SLA commitment doc and the internal incident ticket for your records.

We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience. If you'd like an exec-level call to walk through the post-mortem, I'm happy to coordinate.
